_comment: What ARIA 1.0 ships, pinned by hash, and what it leaves open. release/check.mjs compares it with this repository, the package archives and the site. A candidate may leave decisions pending; the final release may not. Nothing here is published until the owner authorizes each step of the release plan.

edition.label: 1 November 2026
edition.state: the edition of ARIA 1.0: the 7 September 2026 text with §3, §5, §6, §7 and §8 revised as TLF adopted them (D7)

schemas.status: the AID 1.0 credential schema; draft until the issuance cutover
historical: credentials issued before the cutover
ARIA AP receipt (format and retrieval decided under D4)
an issuer key set (D2); the demonstration issuer’s is pinned under trust
historical: ATP, deprecated in favour of ARIA AP
historical: ATP, deprecated in favour of ARIA AP

federation.state: version 1.0.0, adopted by TLF (D7) and implemented by the authority

trust._comment: Trust material an adopter configures explicitly. The SDK trusts no issuer by default. A profile names an issuer, the key set it serves and the fingerprint of that set’s first key (its anchor), which an adopter pins out of band; maxLevel and statusLists are what the profile accepts from it.
trust.production: none yet: production ARIA 1.0 uses a new TLF issuer DID and keys

profiles.guarantee: demonstration: credentials of this issuer are not a production guarantee
profiles.note: the public keys are those the authority deployed on 2026-10-30 signs with (its issuer-keys.json); active_from (2026-10-30, the deployment day) is operator-supplied metadata, outside the pinned fingerprint, confirmed by TLF; the set is served since 2 November 2026

levels.L1: issued where the authority reads domain-binding records and the registry enables it; agent.bar's demonstration issues it, with its identity checks on a provider's sandbox, as no production guarantee

capabilities.credential: AID 1.0, composite ML-DSA-65 + Ed25519 signature, both halves required; status in a signed Bitstring Status List
capabilities.trust: explicit trust profiles in the SDK; no implicit issuer; the demonstration issuer’s key set, pinned by its anchor (see trust)

offered: RFC 9421 signed requests with a per-request challenge
admission with level, scope, delegation depth and human-approval refusal
one execution per operation with aria-ap-receipt/1

decisions.subject: one receipt format with HTTP status and code
refuse without a required approval, for now
the specification stays on the site, mapped to an edition
the current deployment is a demonstration trust domain; production 1.0 uses a new TLF issuer and keys
the demonstration issuer publishes its key set at /v1/keyset; adopters pin its anchor under a profile they name
new issuance: three lower-case segments, no version; 1.0 documents read with two or more; wildcards only in receiver policy, deny prevails
the holder key is ARIA’s own encoding, the raw 32-byte Ed25519 key in base58btc; Multikey adds 0xed01
TLF adopts revisions r3 and r4: the federation contract 1.0.0 and the revised specification sections
package names: @trustlayer-foundation/aria-sdk and @trustlayer-foundation/aria-ap 1.0.0, in the npm organization trustlayer-foundation

retrieval as implemented: a current credential of the same DID with proof of possession, renewed or not, retrieves the original receipts; revocation deletes none and does not prevent historical verification
previousCredentialId kept: it relates a renewal to the credential before it; the DID never changes and verification never walks the chain
the current suite is kept for 1.0; the credential proof metadata is unsigned, and the signed validFrom and validUntil are the dates that count

compatibility: credentials already issued keep their signed bytes, identifiers, context URL and resolution paths
schema/aid-v1.2.json stays published while any credential declaring spec_version 1.2 is valid
@aria-registry/verify 1.x is no longer served by npm (404 since 1 November 2026); the W3C registry entry that cites it must move to the 1.0 packages (INVARIANTS, npm package names)
ATP identifiers stay as deprecated compatibility identifiers: the v=ATP1 record, ATP- codes and the ATP schemas at their URLs
